graph.title: Mail Van
notes: Instruction stickers (7731 / envelope) are not parts and are omitted.

The booklet builds a mailbox model and a van model separately. They are linked in the graph only by the minifig, who is shown holding the mailbox door open (a contact edge, step 4) and later sits on the van seat (contact, step 18).

The inventory prints 9339 (minifig legs) and 9566 (steering wheel on blue stand) as short numbers; they are represented by the real catalogue entries lego-970c00 (black minifig legs) and lego-seat-stand-blue (booklet label 9566).
Mailbox letters are loose and slid into the slot, so they are contact edges.

Catalogue-missing Element IDs from the page 16 inventory were created as new 'lego-<id>' types. The van chassis (4521850) was given many numbered stud/anti-stud ports so each attachment uses its own port.

Stud-level positions of several yellow bricks, mudguards (4 total, only the left side is visible), tail lights and roof plates are inferred from small isometric drawings; some supporting parts are approximations.
Headlight round plate attaches to the headlight brick's side recess; modelled as a side stud on the brick for compatibility.
The two yellow 2x2 plates under the chassis hold the axle plates; the third 2x2 sits in the chassis centre. Wheels are a 4x repeat attached to the axle plate axles via overrides.

graph_initial.title: Mail Van
notes: Instruction stickers (7731 / envelope) are not parts and are omitted.
Page 16 inventory lists some Element IDs not in the catalogue; new part types created with 'lego-<id>'. 9566 steering wheel on plate and 4211110 mailbox post use catalogue entries.

Exact stud-level positions for several yellow bricks, mudguards (4 total, only left side shown), tail lights and roof plates are inferred from small isometric pictures; many 'joined' endpoints use the chassis or a nearby body piece as the supporting part.
The two yellow 2x2 plates under the chassis hold the axle plates; the third 2x2 sits in the chassis centre hole.

Mailbox letters are loose, inserted in the mailbox slot, modelled as contact edges. Minifig sits on the blue seat in the final step; mailbox and van are separate models (mailbox built first, minifig built on page 2).
Wheels are a 4x repeat; the axle plate axle ports are attached via overrides (front axle.1/.2, rear axle.1/.2).
